**Subject: EMA/EMEC actuation for aerospace & defense (new-build + retrofit) | Evidence base: Tier 2 public sources only, no Tier-1 user data | Window: Sept 2021 – Sept 2026 | Compiled 4 Sept 2026**

## Key Insights

- **No "current product" exists to benchmark** — Phase 1 supplied no Tier-1 user data, so Moog's flight-control actuation portfolio is used as the *reference* against Safran, Honeywell, Woodward and Curtiss-Wright (Confidence: High that the gap exists).
- **Feature comparison in this market is asymmetric, not competitive** — Moog and Safran publish detailed application-level capability lists; Honeywell, Woodward and Curtiss-Wright publish almost nothing comparable, so most of their grid cells are *undisclosed*, not *absent* (Confidence: High).
- **Warranty terms, list pricing and like-for-like performance specs are publicly undisclosed by all five vendors** — only one quantified spec surfaced across two research passes, and it predates the analysis window (Confidence: High).
- **Moog and Safran hold structurally different public positions on landing gear**: Moog claims technology-neutral trade studies across all actuation types, while Safran's disclosed high-load landing-gear path is electro-*hydrostatic* (EHA), not electromechanical (Confidence: Medium).
- **Digital/connectivity claims are product-specific, not portfolio-wide** — the only documented cockpit-data feature is Safran's carbon-disk wear reporting on the 787 electric brake (Confidence: Medium).

---

## Reference Product Definition

**UNKNOWN — no current product defined.** The subject brief names a competitor set (Moog, Safran, Honeywell) but no incumbent product, and Phase 1 supplies no CRM, RFQ or product data. Per the comparison requirement, the leading vendors' flagship offerings are compared, with **Moog's flight control and utility actuation portfolio treated as the reference column** — selected because it is the only portfolio in the brief with published application-level coverage spanning military fixed-wing, rotorcraft, commercial and space (Source: Moog "AG Aircraft Capabilities" catalogue via AeroExpo, URL not recorded in brief, undated). *So what:* every comparison below is vendor-to-vendor, not product-to-product, and cannot substitute for a shipset-level technical benchmark.

## Cell Basis — Portfolio & Application Coverage

**FACT (High).** Moog publishes an application list closely matching the subject scope: pilot controls, flight control computers, fly-by-wire systems, primary flight control actuation, leading-edge flap actuation, weapons-bay door drive, **wing-fold actuation**, engine controls and utility actuation for military fixed-wing; PHM and stability augmentation for rotorcraft; side-stick controls and distributed control electronics for commercial/bizjet; TVC and control electronics for launchers (Source: Moog AG Aircraft Capabilities catalogue via AeroExpo, undated; Moog India space page, undated). *So what:* Moog is the only vendor in the brief with published wing-fold actuation, meaning that specific application has no visible public competitor.

**FACT (Medium).** Safran publishes matching or broader coverage in the utility and landing domains: cargo door, nacelle and landing-gear opening, nose wheel, pilot control, rotor brake and air-intake EMAs; complete flap systems including control electronics, power drive unit and wing-tip asymmetry brakes; HSTA; ATA-32 landing gear control units; cockpit control levers (Source: Safran, safran-group.com/products-services/ema-electromechanical-actuators and Safran FCS/product index pages, undated). The Collins acquisition added fighter flight controls, helicopter main/tail-rotor actuators, and missile fin and thrust-vector controls (Source: Janes, 28 Jul 2025; observation date Jul 2025). *So what:* on published breadth, Safran now overlaps Moog across nearly every subject application except wing fold.

**OBSERVATION (Medium).** Honeywell's publicly documented actuation content in this evidence base is confined to missile actuation and electronic control ("Assure", Source: Honeywell/PRNewswire, Mar 2026), a 48-actuator naval linear EMA system (Source: Honeywell product page, undated) and a self-described AAM leadership position (Source: Honeywell product page, undated). *So what:* Honeywell cannot be feature-compared to Moog or Safran on manned-aircraft flight-control actuation from public sources — the absence is a disclosure gap, not evidence of absence.

**FACT (High).** Woodward's actuation entry is the ~$65M-revenue (2024) North American EMA business divested by Safran under US regulatory conditions, which Woodward described as "not financially material" (Sources: Safran press release, safran-group.com, 21 Jul 2025; FlightGlobal, 22 Jul 2025). **FACT (Medium):** Curtiss-Wright's disclosed EMA content is a ~$40M ground-based air-defense award using adapted commercial roller-screw and motor technology (Source: Interesting Engineering, ~Sept 2026). *So what:* both are structurally present in the competitor set but publicly invisible at aircraft-feature level.

## Performance, Warranty and Pricing

**UNKNOWN — insufficient public evidence.** Across two research passes, no vendor published comparable force, stroke, bandwidth or MTBF figures; no warranty terms were disclosed by any of the five; and no list pricing exists. The single quantified specification found is Safran's 787 electric brake weight saving of 141 lb (787-8) / 244 lb (787-9), from a pre-window catalogue (~2018) and therefore usable only as long-term trend evidence. **INTERPRETATION (Medium):** the absence of price lists is consistent with a program-negotiated, non-catalogue market rather than with poor research coverage. *So what:* any competitive positioning built on spec-sheet superiority cannot currently be evidenced from public sources.

## Digital, Connectivity and Sustainability

**FACT (Medium).** Safran's 787 electric brake integrates real-time carbon-disk wear assessment with data transmission to the cockpit, supported by a three-region EBAC avionics repair network (Dallas, Singapore, Massy) (Source: Safran product pages/literature, undated). **FACT (Medium).** Moog lists Prognostics and Health Management within its rotorcraft capability set only. *So what:* health-monitoring is disclosed as a product-level feature at both vendors, not as a portfolio-wide digital platform, so "digital capability" cannot be scored above partial for anyone.

**FACT (Medium).** Safran's only sustainability claim in evidence is that its electric brake is cadmium-, beryllium-, asbestos- and solvent-free through the production cycle (Source: Safran news, 22 Jun 2017 — **staleness flag: pre-window**). Honeywell's naval EMA claim is functional rather than environmental: elimination of hydraulic infrastructure and leaks. *So what:* sustainability is not currently a differentiated, actively-marketed axis in this segment's public material.

## Public Differentiators

**FACT / INTERPRETATION (Medium).** Moog claims technology-neutrality — "extensive experience in all forms of actuation technology… unbiased trade studies" (Source: Moog flight control page, undated); the "technology leader" element is self-assessment, not verified fact. Safran claims full-system flap integration and first-in-service commercial electric brakes on the 787 (~800 aircraft equipped, Source: The BRAKE Report, 21 Nov 2025). *So what:* the two disclosed positions differ in kind — Moog markets architecture-agnostic selection, Safran markets installed-base precedent — which means head-to-head feature scoring understates a positioning difference the grid cannot capture.

## Confidence Summary

Roughly one-third of this report rests on **High**-confidence evidence: the Safran/Collins transaction scope and the forced Woodward divestiture (company press releases, Janes, FlightGlobal), Honeywell Aerospace scale disclosures, and the confirmed absence of warranty/pricing/spec disclosure across all vendors. The bulk of the capability grid rests on **Medium** confidence, because it is built from undated OEM product and catalogue pages — authoritative as to what a vendor claims, but unverifiable as to currency, and not independently corroborated. **Low**-confidence material (the unverified Curtiss-Wright/Liebherr collaboration) has been excluded from the grid entirely. The three dominant knowledge gaps are: (1) no like-for-like performance specifications exist publicly, so no technical superiority claim can be adjudicated; (2) Honeywell's manned-aircraft actuation portfolio is effectively undisclosed, leaving its column structurally incomplete; and (3) no vendor discloses warranty or price, so two required comparison dimensions are empty by evidence, not by omission. Closing these would require Tier-1 user data — RFQ responses, win/loss records, or shipset-level technical submissions.
